scope: feature branch 005-assessment-upload-workflow vs main (git diff main...HEAD, 77 files, +8890/-421); combined correctness+spec-compliance lens (craft-review/craft-simplify) plus the security lens (craft-security) per brief

findings.claim: [security] config/settings.py — the exact module the production Docker image loads (DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE=config.settings, DJANGO_ENV=production) — now hardcodes ALLOWED_HOSTS=["*"], SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE=False and CSRF_COOKIE_SECURE=False unconditionally, with no DEBUG/environment gate. The comment above the block claims 'config/production.py sets its own ALLOWED_HOSTS from the environment', but config/production.py contains no such setting (it only configures AWS S3 storage) and is never loaded as a Django settings module anywhere in the repo. Two lines further down, the pre-existing CSRF_TRUSTED_ORIGINS list comprehension derives from ALLOWED_HOSTS, so this change also turns CSRF_TRUSTED_ORIGINS into ["https://*"] — a netloc of "*" that, once stripped of its leading '*' by Django's suffix-match check, becomes the empty string, which every host trivially satisfies via str.endswith(''), disabling Django's Origin-header CSRF check for every domain. None of this is required by, or mentioned in, spec.md or decisions.md for this feature; it matches this org's own documented pattern for reaching a local WSL2 dev server over the tailnet (AGENTS.md 'devserver'), which appears to have been applied directly to the production settings module by mistake during this run.
findings.evidence: config/settings.py:26-36 (new, unconditional); deploy/Dockerfile:16-17 sets DJANGO_ENV=production and DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE=config.settings for this same file; config/production.py:1-8 defines only AWS_STORAGE_BUCKET_NAME/AWS_S3_ENDPOINT_URL/AWS_S3_CLIENT_CONFIG, no ALLOWED_HOSTS, and is not referenced by any DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE in the repo (grep for 'config.production' across the tree returns nothing); deploy/docker-compose.yml routes the site at portal.heatflow.world through Traefik over TLS (real production deployment); config/settings.py:84-86 (pre-existing, unmodified) is `CSRF_TRUSTED_ORIGINS = [f"https://{domain}" for domain in globals().get("ALLOWED_HOSTS", [])]`. git show main:config/settings.py has no ALLOWED_HOSTS/SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE/CSRF_COOKIE_SECURE lines at all — this is a wholly new, unguarded regression.
findings.reproduction: grep DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE deploy/Dockerfile -> config.settings (the file this diff edited); git diff main...HEAD -- config/settings.py shows the three assignments with no surrounding `if DEBUG` / `if os.environ.get(...)` guard; grep -rln config.production across the repo returns only config/production.py itself, confirming nothing ever loads it as a settings module.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove these three lines from config/settings.py entirely, or gate them explicitly behind a check that is false in the production image, e.g. `if DEBUG: ALLOWED_HOSTS = [...]; SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE = False; CSRF_COOKIE_SECURE = False` — never as unconditional top-level assignments in the module the Dockerfile points DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE at for production.

findings.claim: [correctness] ReviewDescriptionForm.clean() persists a new LiteratureItem as a side effect of Django's full_clean(), which Django always calls after field-level cleaning regardless of whether an earlier field already errored. A submission that supplies a bibliography_file but fails validation on another field (e.g. leaves the required 'reviewers' field empty) still creates and saves an orphaned LiteratureItem to the shared catalogue even though the form as a whole is invalid and no Review is ever created. Because a file input is not resubmitted automatically on redisplay, a user who reattaches the same bibliography file after fixing the other error creates a second, duplicate LiteratureItem — exactly the 'duplicate publication from a bibliography file' edge case spec.md names, except caused by a form-validation defect rather than genuine user error, and with no recovery path.
findings.evidence: project/review/forms.py:91-98 (`clean()` calls `LiteratureItem.objects.create(item=bibliography_data)` unconditionally whenever `literature` is blank and `bibliography_data` is present); Django's Form.full_clean() (site-packages django/forms/forms.py:337-339) calls `self._clean_fields()` then unconditionally `self._clean_form()` -> `self.clean()`, with no short-circuit when `_clean_fields()` already added an error.
findings.reproduction: POST to review-create with a well-formed CSL-JSON `bibliography_file`, `literature` left blank, and `reviewers` omitted (ModelMultipleChoiceField, required=True). `form.is_valid()` returns False (missing reviewers), but `LiteratureItem.objects.count()` has already increased by one before `is_valid()` returns. Resubmitting with `reviewers` filled in and the same bibliography file reattached creates a second LiteratureItem with identical `item` data.
findings.suggested_fix: In `clean()`, only create the LiteratureItem once no other field has already errored, e.g. guard the create with `if not literature and bibliography_data and not self.errors:` before calling `LiteratureItem.objects.create(...)`, deferring the write until the rest of the form is known to be valid.

findings.claim: [documentation] docs/development/testing-standards.md is edited by this diff (its `status`/`Review.STATUS_CHOICES` references are rewritten to `state`/`States`), but the three `Review.objects.create(dataset=dataset, state=States.AWAITING_DECISION)` calls in its 'Workflow Testing Patterns' and 'State-Based Fixture Patterns' examples still omit `literature=`, which is a required (non-null, no-default) OneToOneField on Review. Run as written, each example raises IntegrityError before it reaches the assertions it is meant to demonstrate. The gap predates this diff (`literature` was already required on `main`), but this diff touches these exact lines and the review protocol treats a broken example on a touched documentation page as a verified HIGH finding regardless of when the gap was introduced, since it is a reader's first contact with how to construct a Review in a test.
findings.evidence: docs/development/testing-standards.md — the `test_review_submission_workflow`, `test_full_workflow_import_to_export`, and `test_approve_for_publication_requires_a_data_curator` examples each call `Review.objects.create(dataset=dataset, state=States.AWAITING_DECISION)` with no `literature=` argument; project/review/models.py:79-85 declares `literature = models.OneToOneField("literature.LiteratureItem", ..., on_delete=models.CASCADE, related_name="review")` with no `null=True`/`blank=True`/default.
findings.reproduction: Paste the first example under 'Workflow Testing Patterns' into a `@pytest.mark.django_db` test and run it: `Review.objects.create(dataset=dataset, state=States.AWAITING_DECISION)` raises `django.db.utils.IntegrityError: NOT NULL constraint failed: review_review.literature_id`.
findings.suggested_fix: Add `literature=LiteratureItemFactory()` (matching the factory already used elsewhere in this feature's own tests) to each of the three `Review.objects.create(...)` calls in this file.

findings.claim: [correctness / Constitution Art. V] project/review/models.py, forms.py, views.py and menus.py all import `gettext as _` (eager) and use it for attributes Django evaluates once at import/class-definition time — model `verbose_name`/`help_text`, form field `label`/`help_text`, view `page_title`, and the menu entry's `label` — rather than `gettext_lazy`, which is the correct choice for exactly this class of attribute (Django's own docs give model verbose_name/help_text as the canonical gettext_lazy example). Once the process has imported these modules, the string is permanently fixed to whichever language was active at that moment and will not vary per request/locale afterwards. states.py and admin.py in this same diff use `gettext_lazy` correctly for the equivalent attributes, so the inconsistency is local to four files. No other locale is currently configured (no project `.po` files, no `LANGUAGES` setting), so there is no reachable effect today, but Constitution Article V explicitly requires new UI components to be i18n-ready from introduction and calls retrofitting 'costly and error-prone'.
findings.evidence: project/review/models.py:12 (`gettext as _`) used at models.py:22-106 for every Review/SubmittedFile verbose_name/help_text; project/review/forms.py:12 used at forms.py:26-62 for field labels/help_text; project/review/views.py:12 used at views.py:45,71,105 for page_title; project/review/menus.py:9 used at menus.py:49 for the menu label. Contrast: project/review/states.py:16 and project/review/admin.py:4 both use `gettext_lazy as _` for the same kind of import-time-evaluated attribute.
findings.suggested_fix: Change the translation import in models.py, forms.py, views.py and menus.py to `from django.utils.translation import gettext_lazy as _`, matching states.py and admin.py.
